source.title: Persistent Depth Ordering amid Shifting Block-Bypass Responses in Language Model Pretraining
source.authors: Sheng-Ye Tao; Yin-Zhu Cheng; Hai-Hua Xie

page_placements.theme: Restoration at the level of residual-stream features, directions or activation geometry (not component outputs)

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures whole-block bypass responses and downstream propagation, and reports that matched responses vary with perturbation scale and direction without identifying targeted compensation. This refines how bypass effects should be interpreted, but does not directly establish the claimed restoration of the original prediction.
record.gate_note: The paper reports many block-bypass sensitivity profiles and related training-time analyses. Those results do not measure restoration of the original prediction or the direct effect of an ablated component, so they are not included as self-repair rows. The rows below cover the controlled perturbation and downstream-response results relevant to that question.
record.test_reason: The study bypasses whole Transformer blocks and measures the total output change, local missing-update size, matched-magnitude downstream JS and direction-specific norm attenuation. It never compares an ablated component's direct effect with its total effect, so it does not measure later layers restoring the output (V1) or any other version. Its direction-control test of 'targeted compensation' uses a related but different construct: attenuation of perturbation norm relative to random or permuted directions, not output restoration. The authors state their results do not identify targeted compensation or self-repair, but they do not argue self-repair is absent. The study cites Rushing & Nanda only to position its own metrics.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right but incomplete. The headline finding is that block-bypass sensitivity keeps its depth ordering across pretraining checkpoints, while magnitudes redistribute at recurring, cross-domain-transferable positions. Secondly, local missing-update magnitude and matched downstream response change differently (Pythia vs OLMo-2 7B) and depend on perturbation scale and direction, without identifying targeted compensation or self-repair.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses identity bypass of complete Transformer blocks across training checkpoints, plus matched-magnitude perturbations and direction controls; it does not reproduce attention-layer or head ablation self-repair measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Matched-JS checkpoint trends depend on perturbation strength: Pythia has a positive change at γ = 0.25, an interval including zero at γ = 0.50, and negative changes at γ = 0.75 and 1.00. Directional specificity also differs between random-orthogonal and token-permuted controls.

fits_no_version.finding: In Pythia-160M, the natural missing-update direction is not preferentially attenuated downstream in a way that meets the preregistered targeted-compensation criterion. Specificity is −0.0328 vs random and +0.0276 vs permuted at the final checkpoint, so it depends on the control family.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Downstream layers selectively attenuate the specific residual perturbation produced by bypassing a whole block, more than generic perturbations of equal norm.

fits_no_version.finding: At matched relative perturbation magnitude, Pythia's pooled downstream JS response decreases over pretraining (−0.00262), with a sign that depends on scale (+ at γ=0.25, − at γ≥0.75). OLMo-2 7B's matched and natural JS also decrease.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Pretraining changes downstream sensitivity to block-level residual perturbations, in a scale-dependent way.

fits_no_version.finding: The natural missing-update magnitude from block bypass grows over Pythia training (0.3946→0.5927 relative RMS) but is stable in OLMo-2 7B.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The size of the residual update a block contributes changes over pretraining.

record.problems: The experiments bypass complete blocks rather than isolating attention layers or heads, and do not directly measure restoration of the original prediction against the component’s direct effect. Independent-run replication is concentrated in Pythia-160M; OLMo-2 7B is a single trajectory. Raw token-level activations and acquisition code are outside the summary export.
record.rows_left_out: The broad layer-by-checkpoint and text-domain block-bypass profile results are left out because they report sensitivity and redistribution, not downstream restoration or compensation.

untested.parts: Attention-layer ablation and the restoration of output by later attention layers relative to the ablated layer's direct effect. Only whole-block bypass total effects are measured.
All: late-MLP downregulation of the maximum-likelihood token, and its change under ablation.
All: single-head ablations and compensation on general text.
All: per-prompt compensation fraction and overcorrection.
All: backup heads, copy suppression, LayerNorm rescaling and anti-erasure neurons as self-repair carriers. The final-normalization specificity change is not framed as self-repair.
All: only identity bypass (a zero-update analogue) is used; there are no mean or resample ablations.
All: whether ablation importance scores misstate component function.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T5' with a V1 limits_scope label overreaches. The study never measures restoration of output by later layers, and it does not claim self-repair is absent; it only says its measures do not identify it. The intervention is whole-block identity bypass (attention plus MLP), not attention-layer ablation. No verdicts are given.

versions.untested_parts: Uses complete Transformer-block bypasses rather than attention-layer ablations; does not directly measure later attention layers restoring the original prediction relative to the ablated block’s direct effect.
Late-MLP counterbalancing of the maximum-likelihood token and its change under earlier-component ablation.
Single attention-head ablations and compensation on the full output distribution across model families and sizes.
Promptwise compensation variability and overcorrection beyond the original effect.
Identification of backup heads, copy-suppression heads, final LayerNorm rescaling, or anti-erasure neurons as self-repair mechanisms.
Whether compensation appears under mean or resample ablations rather than identity bypass.
Whether ablation-based importance scores misstate component function.

relation.reason: The related-work discussion connects the intervention pathway to self-repair research, while the study explicitly states that its results do not identify self-repair or targeted compensation.

tranche.reason: Whole-block bypass sensitivity, matched perturbation responses and directional norm attenuation measure related constructs without establishing the attention-layer compensation, head-level repair or other effects specified by V1–V7.

source_check.notes: Failure of the preregistered targeted-compensation criterion does not establish absence of self-repair. Final natural-direction attenuation is stronger than random controls but weaker than permuted controls.

statements.correction: Reproducibility Statement and Appendix A: accompanying package includes analysis code and figure/table code; raw focal acquisition records and acquisition code are outside the summary export.
statements.problem: The numerical and experimental descriptions are correct. The 'code n' designation conflicts with the text's description of accompanying analysis and plotting code.
